You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed, with no visible opening remaining along its closure?
node.criteria: Pass if the jacket's front panels meet along the entire closure and no opening remains. Fail if any visible opening remains along the closure. Unknown if the closure is obscured or the image does not provide enough evidence to determine whether it is fully closed.
node.binding: Assess the same jacket and closure as in s1. Full closure is the requested endpoint; partial closure is not complete fulfillment.

node_traces.evidence: The same jacket remains visibly open in the edited image: its front panel hangs away from her body, leaving an opening along the closure.

dependencies.evidence: The jacket’s front is visibly more open in the edited image, with a panel hanging away from her body, rather than brought together compared with the source.

fulfillment: The node’s target and completion criterion are clear, and the traces are valid visual judgments—not transport or schema failures. The edited image appears to show the jacket hanging more open, while the source already makes the closure difficult to assess; however, the reference label is only an aggregate constraint, not proof that either check is wrong. Investigate the binding and evidence path: ensure s1 compares the same jacket closure in source and edit, and s2 assesses the edited image against “fully closed” without treating a hanging panel alone as conclusive if the closure is obscured. Preserve the distinction between complete, partial progress, absent, and unresolved; do not force “yes” or weaken the full-closure requirement. The fulfillment node depends on both checks, so verify that their evidence supports the progress comparison and final-state decision before mapping two failures to absent. High confidence and repeated agreement are not independent confirmation; if the relevant closure is not visible, route to unknown rather than infer failure.

response.content: {"text":"The binding already identifies the same jacket and the full-closure endpoint, so do not relax that criterion or infer the reference answer. Improve the evidence instruction to require inspecting the actual closure line and whether the front panels meet, rather than treating a panel hanging away from the body as sufficient proof of an opening. In these images the edited figure is turned sideways and the jacket front/closure is largely obscured; the source also does not clearly expose the closure. Route this case to unknown when the closure cannot be seen, rather than making a confident fail judgment. Keep this final-state check distinct from s1’s source-to-edit progress comparison, so downstream fulfillment can distinguish unresolved evidence from no progress. The traces are valid executions, not transport or schema failures; the aggregate reference label is a constraint, not atomic proof that the jacket is closed."}
